entries.x: Business processes Two processes (BPMN 2.0 with diagram interchange) in input/business-processes/ , checked with bun run cat bpmn:detangle (layout) and drawn with the platform's renderer. Adjudication: pending (Clinical SME; programme SME for MEASLES.B). MEASLES.A — Measles vaccination contact Lanes: client and caregiver; health worker. A client at any health contact (fixed site, outreach, school, or a visit for something else) brings a home-based record if there is one. The health worker retrieves the history, counts the recorded doses (DT.03), determines the dose due (DT.01, and DT.04 for a child living with HIV on HAART), screens (DT.02), gives MCV, records it with the next due date, or records why not and when to return. Rests on: the per-client recommendations of Table 1's measles footnote and Table 3's measles row; the catch-up guide's practices on records, validity, spacing and return dates. Serves user scenarios S1–S4. MEASLES.B — Defaulter tracking and coverage reporting Lanes: programme manager; data manager; health worker. Monthly, the programme manager lists children overdue for MCV1 or MCV2 and zero-dose children; health workers remind caregivers and reach them (they then go through MEASLES.A); the data manager aggregates MCV doses and computes the indicators; the programme manager reviews coverage and dropout; the data manager reports annually on the Joint Reporting Form. Rests on: catch-up guide catchup.defaulter-tracking , catchup.mcv2-only-after-mcv1 ; JRF 2016. Serves user scenario S5. Not drawn Recommendations acted on outside a client contact have no process here: national schedule and policy decisions ( measles.two-doses-standard , measles.mcv2-in-schedule , measles.policies-allow-older-ages , measles.mcv2-at-school-entry , measles.same-formulation-both-doses , catchup.national-catch-up-schedule ) and the health-worker immunity condition ( measles.health-worker-immunity ). They configure MEASLES.A (DE.06, the schedule setting) or are listed in the gap report.

User scenarios The journeys the processes and decision tables serve, told as stories. The 42 scenario candidates written at L1 (one per recommendation or practice, under l1-extractions/ /scenarios/ ) are grouped here into the four journeys a measles programme runs. Names are made up. Adjudication: pending (Clinical SME). MEASLES.S1 — A routine first and second dose Asha is 9 months old and lives where measles still circulates. Her mother brings her and her home-based record to the clinic. The health worker reads the record: no MCV yet. Asha is well, has had no other live vaccine in the last four weeks, and has no history of allergy to the vaccine. The health worker gives MCV1, records it with the date, and writes the return date for MCV2 at 15 months. At 15 months Asha returns; at least four weeks have passed, so she gets MCV2 and her measles series is complete. Rests on: measles.mcv1-9-months-high-transmission , measles.mcv2-15-18-months , measles.mcv-minimum-interval , measles.live-vaccine-spacing , measles.contraindications , catchup.multi-dose-return-date . MEASLES.S2 — An older child who missed doses Daniel is 6 years old and comes to the clinic for a cough. The health worker uses the visit to check his vaccination status. His caregiver has no home-based record and the register holds none, so the health worker assumes he is unvaccinated and offers MCV. He gets his first dose today and is told to return in four weeks for the second; no booster follows. Rests on: measles.catch-up-every-opportunity , measles.routine-delivery-not-age-limited , catchup.every-touchpoint , catchup.unconfirmed-assume-unvaccinated , measles.interrupted-delayed-schedule-row . MEASLES.S3 — An infant at high risk Lina is 7 months old, born to a mother living with HIV, during a measles outbreak in her district. The health worker gives a supplementary dose and records it as MCV0. It does not count towards her routine doses: she still gets MCV1 and MCV2 at the scheduled ages. Rests on: measles.mcv0-situations , measles.mcv0-recording , measles.mcv0-then-routine-doses , measles.hiv-exposed-mcv0 . MEASLES.S4 — A client who should not be vaccinated today Grace, 24, asks for a measles vaccine before starting work at a hospital, which requires proof of measles immunity. She is pregnant. The health worker does not vaccinate her now and records the reason; she can be vaccinated after the pregnancy. Rests on: measles.avoid-in-pregnancy , measles.health-worker-immunity . MEASLES.S5 — Finding children who are behind Each month the programme manager at a health facility reviews the register for children whose MCV1 or MCV2 is overdue, and for zero-dose children in the catchment area, and arranges reminders and outreach. The data manager counts MCV1 and MCV2 doses by age group, never recording a dose as MCV2 for a child without MCV1, and reports coverage on the Joint Reporting Form.
